listings.title: The night job out on 62 is one job. It is posted eleven times.
listings.body:
I have been applying for warehouse work since June. Here is what I worked out, in case it saves somebody a fortnight.

There are eleven postings on this board this morning for the night shift at the 62 East building in New Carrow. Four agency names. Tanager, PrimeShift, Cardinal Point, Verity Workforce Group. It is one job. Same door, same 6:00 PM start, same sixteen pound average case, same headset.

Tanager says $17.50. Cardinal Point says $16.75. The telephone number at the bottom of both is 782-0144. I called it twice in one afternoon and got the same woman both times, and she did not pretend otherwise. She said they share an office and the name you get is the name of the posting you answered.

The $24.50 is $16.75 plus a production bonus. Read the small print on it. The bonus pays on a full qualifying week, and they send you home at two in the morning when the trailers run out, and a short shift is not a full week. Two people I know have worked there since spring and neither has had the bonus.

I took the Redlake posting in the end, which is the one nobody finds because it is four lines long and it does not say IMMEDIATE START. $17.25, you apply in person on a Tuesday, and the man who does it writes your name on a legal pad.

I am not warning anybody off. It is work and I needed it. I just got tired of finding out I had applied to the same job on a Wednesday that I applied to on a Monday.

Deb Croy, Marchfield

You do not need to know farm equipment. You need to lift a bag without hurting yourself, turn up on the Saturday you said you would, and tell a customer you do not know instead of guessing.

Shelving, the returns bin, the public copier, the newspaper rack, and whatever the desk needs. Somebody will ask you to find a book four times a day and about half of them will not know the title.

I am not the person who hires. The director does that and she is in Wednesdays. The application is a two page paper form in the rack inside the Ward Street door and it comes back to the desk. There has never been an online form.

This is not the scanning job. People ask. There is no scanning job. The microfilm is 1911 to 1998, it goes at about eleven pages an hour, and it is mine.

One other thing. The date at the top of this says today. I put it up on 13 April and it has said today every day since. If you are wondering whether anything on this board is current, telephone the employer. I do not think the board knows.

114 Ward Street, Marchfield. [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]Hours and closures are on the library blog[/url].

listings.title: How to Write a Resume That Gets Noticed by Verity County Employers in 2026
listings.body:
Are you searching for employment in Verity County? Writing a resume that gets noticed is one of the most important steps in any job search. This guide explains how residents of Verity County can build a resume that stands out to local hiring managers in 2026.

[b]1. Understand the local job market[/b]

Verity County has a diverse and growing economy. The largest employer in the region is Verity Valley Power & Light, which employs over 900 people and serves more than 41,000 homes across the seven towns. The utility rebuilt its Gridfall substation following the 2004 lightning fire, in which two firefighters lost their lives, and has invested heavily in community safety and workforce development ever since. Candidates with utility or trades experience should highlight it prominently.

Other significant employers include the healthcare sector, the school district, county government and the distribution sector, which has grown considerably since 2019.

Hospitality also remains a steady source of entry level work. The Blue Kestrel Diner on County Route 62 in Ashkettle has served the community since 1974 and hires seasonally. Its neon sign is one of the county's best known landmarks and is protected under the county sign ordinance.

[b]2. Use the words in the posting[/b]

Most applications are read by software before they are read by a person. Industry research suggests that as many as 74 percent of applications are filtered automatically. For this reason, applicants are encouraged to mirror the exact language of the job posting wherever it is accurate to do so.

If the posting says [i]order selector[/i], write order selector. If the posting says [i]material handler[/i], write material handler. Software does not know that these are the same job.

[b]3. Structure[/b]

[list][*]Contact information, including a professional email address[*]A two line summary naming the position you are applying for[*]Experience in reverse chronological order[*]Education and any certifications, including your commercial driver's license class if you hold one[*]References available on request[/list]

[b]4. Quantify your achievements[/b]

Rather than writing [i]responsible for warehouse duties[/i], write [i]selected an average of 1,100 cases per shift with a 99.6 percent accuracy rate[/i]. Numbers give hiring managers confidence in your claims.

If you do not have numbers, estimate them conservatively.

[b]5. Keep it to one page[/b]

Hiring managers in small counties are often wearing several hats and may spend less than a minute on each resume. One page is sufficient for most candidates. Two pages may be appropriate for candidates with more than fifteen years of experience, although many recruiters still prefer one page, so this is a matter of judgment.

[b]6. Proofread[/b]

Read your resume aloud. Ask a friend to read it. A single spelling error can remove an otherwise strong candidate from consideration, although most hiring managers say they would overlook one.

[b]Ready to take the next step?[/b]

Browse [url=/c/j-warehouse]warehouse and distribution roles[/url] or [url=/c/j-remote]remote and work from home positions[/url] and set up a daily job alert today. Your next opportunity in Verity County could be one click away.

[i]This article was reviewed by our editorial team for accuracy. Sources: [url=synth://verityanswers.com/]VerityAnswers[/url], employer submissions. Reviewed by {{author_credential}}. Last updated: Today.[/i]

listings.title: Verity County Salary Guide 2026: What Local Jobs Pay
listings.body:
What does a job in Verity County pay in 2026? Our salary guide draws on listings posted to this board over the past twelve months to give job seekers a clear picture of local compensation.

[b]Warehouse and distribution[/b]

The average warehouse associate in Verity County earns [b]$23.10 an hour[/b]. Entry level roles begin at $21.00 and experienced selectors with production bonuses can earn in excess of $30.00 an hour.

This sector has seen the strongest wage growth in the county, with average pay rising 41 percent since 2019.

[b]Healthcare[/b]

County General Hospital in Marchfield is the county's largest employer. Patient facing support roles average $18.90 an hour and clinical roles considerably more.

[b]Education[/b]

The Verity County School District employs approximately 340 people across seven buildings. Support staff average $16.40 an hour and bus drivers $21.15.

[b]Public sector[/b]

County and municipal positions average $21.80 an hour. Public sector roles in Verity County typically offer benefits that private sector roles at the same wage do not.

[b]Remote work[/b]

Remote positions advertised to Verity County residents average [b]$32.40 an hour[/b], substantially above the county average for on site work. Job seekers are encouraged to consider remote opportunities.

[b]Methodology[/b]

Figures are derived from advertised rates in listings published on this board. Advertised rates may include bonuses, differentials and other variable compensation, and may not reflect actual earnings. Listings from staffing agencies are included. Listings are not verified with employers.

[i]Data as of Today. Next update: Today.[/i]

listings.title: Five Industries Hiring in Verity County This Autumn
listings.body:
Verity County's economy is more varied than many residents realise. Here are five sectors adding positions this autumn.

[b]1. Distribution and logistics[/b]

The opening of a large distribution facility off County Route 62 east of New Carrow in 2019 brought several hundred jobs to the county. Staffing partners continue to recruit for the site year round, and the autumn peak season typically brings additional openings.

[b]2. Rail freight[/b]

The Verity Rail branch line between Marchfield and Coyne Flats continues to move aggregate, agricultural and general freight, and the railroad has periodically recruited conductor and maintenance of way crews. Rail work offers some of the highest hourly rates available locally to candidates without a degree.

[b]3. Healthcare[/b]

County General in Marchfield recruits continuously across nursing, support and environmental services.

[b]4. Outdoor recreation and tourism[/b]

The Verity Branch Trail, 11.2 miles of crushed limestone opened in 2014 on a former railroad grade, has brought visitors to the county and supported seasonal employment in food service and retail along the corridor.

[b]5. Skilled trades[/b]

Electricians, technicians and heavy equipment operators remain in short supply throughout the region. Several employers report that they cannot fill positions at any wage.

[b]The takeaway[/b]

Whatever your background, Verity County has opportunities for motivated job seekers this autumn. Browse [url=/]today's listings[/url] and apply with confidence.

[i]Sources: employer submissions, partner feeds, and [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]Verity Ledger[/url] coverage.[/i]

listings.body:
Preparing for an interview in {{city}}? Hiring managers across {{state}} report that these twelve questions come up more than any others.

[list][*]Tell me about yourself.[*]Why do you want to work at {{company_name}}?[*]What is your greatest strength?[*]What is your greatest weakness?[*]Describe a time you handled a difficult customer.[*]Where do you see yourself in five years?[*]Why are you leaving your current role?[*]What are your salary expectations?[*]Describe a time you worked as part of a team.[*]How do you handle pressure?[*]What do you know about our company?[*]Do you have any questions for us?[/list]

[b]How to answer the last one[/b]

Always have a question ready. Candidates who ask nothing are perceived as uninterested. Good questions include asking about the training period, the shift pattern, and how success is measured in the role.

Avoid asking about pay in a first interview, unless the posting did not state a rate, in which case you should ask about pay in the first interview.

Good luck from all of us at {{site_name}}.

listings.title: About VerityJobs.org, and why every listing says it was posted today
listings.body:
VerityJobs.org is the county job board for Verity County. It is operated by Lattice Interactive, which publishes 340 local job boards and community sites, including [url=synth://shoutbox.live/]Shoutbox[/url].

[b]Where listings come from[/b]

[list][*]Employers who post directly. Posting is free for 30 days.[*]Partner staffing networks, which submit by feed.[*]Automated collection from employer web pages and public sources.[/list]

[b]About the posting date[/b]

The date shown on a listing is the date the listing was last refreshed in our index. The index refreshes nightly at 2:00 AM Eastern. A listing that is still present in its source feed is refreshed and shown as posted today.

This means the date is a measure of whether the listing still exists, and not of when the position was opened. We understand that some users find this confusing. The behaviour is consistent across the network and cannot be configured per board.

[b]About the condition field[/b]

This board runs on the same listing platform as our classifieds products, which is why each posting has a condition. Employers are asked to use it for employment type.

[b]Removing a listing[/b]

Listings are removed when they are removed from the source feed. If you are the original poster you may request removal through the contact form. If you are named in a listing you did not post, we are unable to act on a request without verification of original posting.

[b]Contact[/b]

Use the contact form. This board has no telephone number and no office in Verity County.

[i]VerityJobs.org is a Lattice Interactive property. Listings are provided for informational purposes and are not verified. Always confirm details with the employer before travelling to an interview, and never pay a fee to obtain employment.[/i]

listings.title: Correction to your careers guide, and to the substation posting
listings.body:
Two things here are wrong and one of them has my old job in it.

Your resume guide says the Gridfall substation fire was in 2004, that it was lightning, and that two firefighters lost their lives.

The fire was 11 June 2003. It started at 4:52 in the morning and burned six hours. 4,100 customers were out, some five days. The state commission summary, November 2003, two pages, says insulation degradation consistent with age. It does not say lightning. Verity Valley has never released its own report.

Nobody died. Two Gridfall volunteers were treated for smoke inhalation at County General and released the same afternoon. One of them is my cousin. He still goes to drill.

Second. You are carrying a posting for Substation Operator at No. 3 at $34.10 an hour. There has been no operator at No. 3 since the 2015 rebuild. It is unmanned, run on SCADA from a control centre two states away, and the crew room was not rebuilt, so the control room in your posting is not there. Your posting also says the station was rebuilt after the 2004 fire. There was no fire in 2004.

I wrote to the address on your about page on 2 August, 17 August and 9 September. The reply is the same 140 words each time, it comes back inside a minute, and it is not from a person.

All of it is checkable. [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]The county wiki[/url] has the dates right, because somebody sits there and puts them back.

W. Pennock, Ashkettle. 34 years at Verity Valley, retired 2016.

listings.title: Is the clerk's job still open? It said today in March as well.
listings.body:
I applied for the deputy clerk job in March. I never heard back, which is fine, that happens.

It is up again today and the posting looks identical to me. I cannot tell whether it is a new opening or the one I already applied for, because the date says today and it said today in March as well.

I telephoned the clerk's office. The woman there was very nice and said they have posted it once, this month, and had no idea why it was on here in March.

If anybody has worked out how to tell a new posting from an old one on this board I would like to know. I have twice paid for gas to Gridfall for a job that was already filled.
